subject: Novasys onboarding — model shortlist, context and token estimates
messages:
From: Olivia Hansen <olivia@novasys.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ethan Rowe <ethan.rowe@novasys.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff — model selection & sizing for Novasys MVP

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the intro — excited to get started. We’re planning an internal pilot that will:
- Surface answers from our product documentation and search index
- Run an interactive assistant for sales and support agents
Couple of asks ahead of our kickoff next week:
1) Can you send a recommended shortlist of models (and expected latency/cost differences) for these two modes: search-extraction (short prompts, heavy retrieval) and conversation (agent assist, sometimes long context)?
2) We need a token-volume estimate for a 90-day pilot. Our initial user estimate is ~600 daily active agents, average 40 sessions/day, average 150 input tokens. There will be spikes during launches — want to understand required headroom.
3) Context needs: some workflows will require 4k–6k context for multi-step threads. Is that feasible with your hosted service?

I attached a small sample of logs and a product doc PDF. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.

Thanks,
Olivia
Head of Product
Novasys
(attachment: novasys_product_samples.zip)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Hansen <olivia@novasys.com>, Ethan Rowe <ethan.rowe@novasys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-27T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff — model selection & sizing for Novasys MVP

Hi Olivia — thanks for the summary and the samples. Quick replies inline and a proposed shortlist below.

Shortlist (recommend starting with tiered canary):
- Redwood-Base-8B (fp16): best latency at small context, strong cost/quality tradeoff. Good for search-extraction mode.
- Redwood-Prod-13B (q4_0): higher quality for multi-step reasoning and long context (up to 8k tested); expect ~1.4x latency vs 8B but significantly better coherence.
- Redwood-Economy-3B (q4_0): fallback for high-throughput burst routing (cheapest).

Context and latency notes:
- 2k context: median p50 token latency ~65ms on our hosted API for 8B; 13B ~95ms.
- 6k context: latency grows ~1.6x compared to 2k for 8B; larger models see similar multipliers depending on kernel paths.

90-day pilot token estimate (conservative):
- Base assumptions you shared: 600 DAU * 40 sessions/day * 150 input tokens = 3.6M input tokens/day.
- If we assume average completion = 200 tokens and 60% of sessions call the model: additional ~2.88M output tokens/day.
- Total tokens/day ≈ 6.5M => ~195M tokens/month.
- Peak headroom: plan for 2.5x burst factor during launches => design for ~16M tokens/day.

Quick cost guidance (hosted, non-enterprise list):
- Redwood-Base-8B: ~$7 per 1M tokens (combined in/out) at current public tiers; 13B ~ $12/1M tokens. These are starting points — dedicated/reserved pricing will change with commitments.

Attachments: I attached a token profile snapshot I’ll use to build a capacity sketch.

Next steps:
- Can we confirm the session mix (what % are retrieval-heavy vs long-thread assists)?
- If yes, I’ll loop Marcus to produce a compact capacity + cost sketch and Ben to propose a mutual action plan for rollout.

Happy to discuss on the kickoff — suggest Tue 6/29 10:00–11:00 PT.

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
(attachment: token_profile_snapshot.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-28T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff — model selection & sizing for Novasys MVP

Looping in operational items and the MAP draft. High level notes for the kickoff: 
- Canary plan: start 100 qps to Redwood-Base-8B for search flows; route 10% of agent-assist traffic to Redwood-Prod-13B for quality checks.
- Caching: recommend prefix + retrieval kv-cache for search-extraction flows. We can set a 12-hour cache TTL for repeated docs which will dramatically reduce token spend.
- Quantization: if latency is a hard constraint, run Redwood-Prod-13B in q4 and enable kernel fusion; we’ve validated throughput on our dedicated pools.
- Rollout checkpoints: quality gate (P99 response correctness on eval set), latency gate (P50/P95 within SLA), cost gate (monthly spend vs projected).

Attached: Novasys_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf (draft) — includes milestones, owner matrix, and a proposed 45-day canary timeline.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Field Infra
Redwood Inference
(attachment: Novasys_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.pdf)

Thanks Priya/Ben — this is really helpful. A few clarifications before the call: 
- Session mix: roughly 70% retrieval-heavy (short prompts + doc snippets), 30% agent-assist (back-and-forth, may hit 6k windows occasionally).
- Average output token for retrieval flows is smaller (~40 tokens) vs 200 for agent-assist. Can you re-run the token estimate with 70/30 split?
- SLA question: what P95 latency SLO can we expect for the 13B q4 path under typical load? We need to include targets in the MAP.

Also: when you mention cache TTL and prefix caching, is that something we configure in the initial integration or a later optimization? If configurability is first-class, we can plan to ship a simple config toggle to our agent UI.

Appreciate it — see you on Tue.

—Ethan

Novasys

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Kickoff — model selection & sizing for Novasys MVP

Thanks Ethan — quick updated numbers and plan below (quoting for thread continuity):

> "Session mix: roughly 70% retrieval-heavy (short prompts + doc snippets), 30% agent-assist (back-and-forth, may hit 6k windows occasionally)."

Revised 90-day pilot estimate with 70/30 split: 
- Retrieval-heavy: 600 DAU * 40 sessions/day * 0.7 * 150 input tokens = 3.78M input tokens/day. Output (avg 40) ≈ 0.67M tokens/day.
- Agent-assist: 600 * 40 * 0.3 * 150 = 1.08M input tokens/day. Output (avg 200) ≈ 1.3M tokens/day.
- Total ≈ 6.85M tokens/day => ~206M tokens/month.
- Peak headroom target (2.5x) => plan for ~17M tokens/day peak.

SLA/latency target proposal for MAP (P95 under steady load):
- Redwood-Base-8B (2k contexts): P95 <= 320ms.
- Redwood-Prod-13B (6k contexts, q4): P95 <= 650ms (can tighten on Dedicated).

Cache/config guidance: prefix + doc-level KV cache is a step-one optimization and configurable via our integration flags — we can ship with caching disabled and enable via a feature flag in week 2 of the pilot. That will be on the MAP timeline.

Marcus — can you produce a concise capacity sketch (capacity table: qps, tokens/day, estimated monthly cost by model tier) and one-slide summary for the Tue call? Aim for a quick turnaround this afternoon so I can include in the kickoff notes.

Thanks all — see you on the call.

Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
